title: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.isIso_poincareMap
statement: Let l be a prime and k a field of characteristic p>0 with p != l. Let X, S be separated schemes of finite type over Spec k (objects of Over (Spec k)) and p:X\to S a morphism over k whose underlying morphism of schemes is smooth of pure relative dimension d (d in N). Write Qlb for the condensed ring Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj l and D^b_c(T)[[Qlb]] for the bounded constructible derived category of Qlb-module objects on the pro-etale site of T, with exactly the upstream boundedConstructible predicate [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-complexes, def-sfb-constructible-module] (bounded cohomology and one finite stratification on which each cohomology module is pro-etale locally finitely presented), a monoidal closed full subcategory of the ambient derived category (isMonoidal_boundedConstructible, isMonoidalClosed_boundedConstructible), with unit Qlb_T and internal hom RHom. On it Lp^* -| Rp_* (boundedConstructibleUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction) and Rp_! -| Rp^! (boundedConstructibleUpperShriekAdjunction, Rp^! = boundedConstructibleUpperShriek built from a Nagata compactification), and PF^!: Rp_! K (x) B \to  Rp_!(K (x) Lp^* B) is the derived exceptional projection morphism (boundedConstructibleExceptionalProjection). Qlb_X(d)[2d] = boundedConstructibleTateTwist l X d (2d) is the shift by 2d of the Tate twist tateTwistDerived X l d [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists], bounded constructible by [nt-target-poincare-tate-bc], and pur_p: Rp^! Qlb_S ~= Qlb_X(d)[2d] (boundedConstructibleSmoothPurityIso) is the preimage under the fully faithful inclusion D^b_c \to  D of the chosen smooth purity isomorphism smoothPurityIso l p d [nt-target-smooth-purity-qbar]. The Poincare duality morphism PD_p: Rp_* Qlb_X(d)[2d] \to  RHom(Rp_! Qlb_X, Qlb_S) (poincareMap) is the composite of Rp_*(pur_p^{-1}), Rp_* of the identification Rp^! Qlb_S \to  RHom(Qlb_X, Rp^! Qlb_S) (transpose of the left unitor) and the Verdier exchange morphism Phi_{p,K,L}: Rp_* RHom(K, Rp^! L) \to  RHom(Rp_! K, L) at K=Qlb_X, L=Qlb_S, where Phi is the transpose of the pairing Rp_! K (x) Rp_* RHom(K,Rp^! L) \to  Rp_!(K (x) Lp^* Rp_* RHom(K,Rp^! L)) \to  Rp_!(K (x) RHom(K,Rp^! L)) \to  Rp_! Rp^! L \to  L (PF^!, the counit of Lp^* -| Rp_*, evaluation, the counit of Rp_! -| Rp^!). The trace Tr_p: Rp_! Qlb_X(d)[2d] \to  Qlb_S (trace) is Rp_!(pur_p^{-1}) followed by the counit of Rp_! -| Rp^!, and the compact-support cup product cup_c: Rp_! Qlb_X (x) Rp_* Qlb_X(d)[2d] \to  Rp_! Qlb_X(d)[2d] (cupProduct) is PF^!, Rp_!(Qlb_X (x) counit of Lp^* -| Rp_*) and the left unitor. Then PD_p is an isomorphism in D^b_c(S)[[Qlb]] (Poincare duality). Upstream deduces it from isIso_verdierExchange of WeilConjectures.PoincareDuality.Verdier (Verdier duality: Phi_{p,K,L} is an isomorphism for all bounded constructible K, L, from the derived projection formula isIso_boundedConstructibleExceptionalProjection_app_app by the Yoneda argument Verdier.isIso_exchange_of_isIso), since the other two factors of PD_p are isomorphisms. The upstream statement does not use the smoothness instance (omitted), but PD_p is built from pur_p, whose definition needs it.

proof.text: Work entirely in the target's condensed categories C_T = D_cons(T,Qlb). Write F=Rp_!, U=Lp^*, G=Rp_* and V=Rp^!, and write H_T for the restricted internal Hom. By [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors] and [def-sfb-dc-tensor-hom-adjunction], U is left adjoint to G and A tensor - is left adjoint to H_T(A,-) in these full subcategories. By [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek], F is left adjoint to V on the same categories. Thus every object and Hom set in the following argument lies in C_X or C_S; no comparison with the common-stage Qlb category is being assumed.

proof.text:
Use the target's chosen compactification $p=q\circ j:X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow q S$. By [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek], $F=Rq_*j_!$; by [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors], $j_!K,Lq^*B$ are bounded constructible and $U\cong Lj^*Lq^*$ by the specified composition comparison. The definition of $PF^!$ is the proper projection arrow followed by $Rq_*$ of the inverse open projection and this composition comparison:
$$Rq_*j_!K\otimes B\longrightarrow Rq_*(j_!K\otimes Lq^*B)\xrightarrow{Rq_*(q_{j,K,Lq^*B}^{-1})}Rq_*j_!(K\otimes Lj^*Lq^*B).$$
Here the module-object proper arrow is adjoint to $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\delta_q$, whereas the open map $q_j$ is adjoint to $\mu_j(\eta_K\otimes1)$. By [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison], the actual module-object $\delta_q$, its inverse lax map $\mu_j$, the derived adjunctions and the tensor/pullback identifications agree with the ringed-topos structures. Thus the proper arrow is exactly the map $\alpha$ to which clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational] applies. It is invertible. By [lem-pd-condensed-open-exceptional-projection-formula], the displayed canonical $q_j$, including its use of the actual lax structure, is invertible. Applying $Rq_*$ to its inverse preserves its inverse identities. Composing these two isomorphisms with $Lj^*Lq^*\cong Lp^*$ proves invertibility and naturality of this specified $PF^!_{K,B}$. All objects and inverse morphisms are in the full bounded-constructible subcategories by the cited restriction statements.

proof.text:
Fix K=Qlb_X and L=Qlb_S, and put E=G H_X(K,VL) and D=H_S(FK,L). For every B in C_S there is a bijection b_B:Hom_S(B,E) → Hom_S(B,D), formed by the following chain in this direction:
Hom_S(B,G H_X(K,VL)) = Hom_X(UB,H_X(K,VL)) = Hom_X(K tensor UB,VL) = Hom_S(F(K tensor UB),L) = Hom_S(FK tensor B,L) = Hom_S(B,H_S(FK,L)).
The first and third equalities are the two geometric adjunction bijections; the second and fifth are the tensor-Hom adjunction bijections of [def-sfb-dc-tensor-hom-adjunction]. The fourth precomposes with the isomorphism PF_{K,B} from Step 2. The cited restricted adjunctions justify each change of Hom set. They apply to all B in C_S, including E and D, since their functors and internal Hom have codomains C_T. The chain is natural in B because its constituent adjunction bijections and PF are natural.

proof.text:
The bijection b_B is postcomposition with the specified exchange Phi:E → D, not merely with some isomorphism of these objects. Write epsilon:UG → id and epsilon!:FV → id for the two counits. For h:B → E the chain sends h to the tensor-Hom transpose of
FK tensor B --PF_{K,B}-→ F(K tensor UB) --F(1_K tensor (epsilon_{H_X(K,VL)} composed with U(h)))-→ F(K tensor H_X(K,VL)) --F(ev)-→ FVL --epsilon!_L-→ L.
Naturality of PF in B rewrites the first two arrows as (1_{FK} tensor h), followed by PF_{K,E}, followed by F(1_K tensor epsilon_{H_X(K,VL)}). The remaining evaluation and epsilon! arrows are unchanged. This is exactly the pairing used in the target to define Phi, precomposed with 1_{FK} tensor h; naturality of currying therefore gives b_B(h)=Phi composed with h. No duality comparison of coefficient categories is used.

proof.text: Since postcomposition with Phi is bijective on every Hom_S(B,-) by Steps 3-4, Phi is invertible. Explicitly, surjectivity for B=D gives r:D → E with Phi composed with r=id_D. Then Phi composed with (r composed with Phi)=Phi=Phi composed with id_E, and injectivity for B=E gives r composed with Phi=id_E. Thus r is a two-sided inverse. This is the elementary representability argument, with the inverse and both identities written out.

proof.text: Let T=Qlb_X(d)[2d]. The target's pur_p:VQlb_S ~= T is the bounded-constructible preimage of the smooth purity isomorphism supplied by [nt-target-smooth-purity-qbar]. Its inverse T → VQlb_S is therefore invertible. Applying G preserves its inverse identities, giving an isomorphism GT → G VQlb_S. The target already supplies T as an object of C_X through [nt-target-poincare-tate-bc]. Its current hypothesis that l is invertible on X holds here: the image of l in the field k is nonzero since char(k) differs from l, so its inverse in k pulls back to an inverse in every structure sheaf of a k-scheme. Its conclusion uses precisely the upstream boundedConstructible predicate of the target; no new choice of purity or of normalization is made.

For A=VQlb_S, the unit-Hom map u:A → H_X(Qlb_X,A), the transpose of the left unitor Qlb_X tensor A → A, is an isomorphism. Indeed, for any B, adjunction identifies postcomposition Hom(B,A) → Hom(B,H_X(Qlb_X,A)) with h mapping to h composed with the unitor on Qlb_X tensor B, which is a bijection with inverse precomposition by the inverse unitor. The same explicit inverse argument of Step 5 makes u invertible; applying G preserves this. By the target's definition, PD_p is G(pur_p inverse), then G(u), then Phi at K=Qlb_X,L=Qlb_S. All three factors are isomorphisms by Steps 5-6 and the present argument, so their composite PD_p is an isomorphism.
